title: Going to Chicago with Fletcher, his marriage and the cold
summary: He took seventy dollars, married the same day, and walked through frozen Chicago to rehearsal with Chu.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So we got ready to go to Chicago. I didn't want to leave New York. I ended up getting a little bit more money than he was willing to pay. I got five dollars more. I think everybody was supposed to get... I don't know, to tell you the truth. He said everybody else was getting fifty-five or sixty, or something like that, and he gave me seventy. So you know, he could tell me anything. But anyway, when he came up with that seventy dollars, I decided to go.

Then when we got to the train station, Thigpen wasn't there. But Dick Vance was there. And he looked kind of strange, because he was... We were all whistling, you know how they do in the band, me and Buster and the (?) people. We was just going... I got married that same day, too. I got married that day, and it was very lucky, going to Chicago... We told the conductor... You know, because we was in the coach. And he gave us one of those staterooms; they called them staterooms. He gave us one of those staterooms, and didn't charge us nothing for it, which I thought was very nice.
When we got there, it was about 26 below. Whew! Man,

we were staying at the Grand Hotel, and me and Chu tried to walk to the Grand Terrace for the rehearsal, you know... Man, we started... Those walks in Chicago are long, baby, believe me. Every block is like four blocks everywhere else. And we walked... We were at 51st and South Parkway, and we had to go to Oakwood Boulevard, that's 39th and Oakwood Boulevard. Well, we was stopping in every place we could find to stop in. Man, my balls were froze!
